wording.title: Regulated Efficacy Claims Require Proof
wording.instruction: A claim breaks this rule if it asserts a specific, measurable, or absolute health, cosmetic, or therapeutic outcome (e.g., curing, preventing, reducing, or changing skin/teeth) without attached evidence and compliance sign-off. This includes vague but definitive promises like 'effective from day one' or 'perfect protection.' A claim is allowed only if it describes a general mode of action or difference (e.g., 'new mode of action') without promising a specific result, or if the required proof is present.
examples_good: A new approach to skincare that works differently than traditional methods.
Contains ingredients known for their antioxidant properties.
Designed to help maintain skin hydration.
examples_bad: Clinically proven to remove wrinkles in 7 days.
Prevents acne and clears blemishes instantly.
Guaranteed to whiten teeth in just one use.

wording.title: Regulated Efficacy Claims Require Proof
wording.instruction: Do not use phrases that promise specific medical, cosmetic, or physical results (such as curing conditions, changing appearance, or outperforming competitors) unless you have a matching factual basis and compliance sign-off. Claims based on robust, verifiable survey data or third-party rankings are allowed without this specific sign-off. Avoid vague or absolute promises of transformation, healing, or superiority that lack documented evidence.
examples_good: Rated #1 by 90% of users in our 2023 customer survey.
Contains 5% niacinamide to support skin barrier function.
Recommended by dermatologists in the UK based on independent clinical trials.
examples_bad: Removes all wrinkles in just 7 days.
More effective than any other toothpaste on the market.
Guaranteed to grow new hair and stop dandruff instantly.

wording.title: Regulated Efficacy Claims Require Evidence and Sign-off
wording.instruction: A sentence breaks this rule when it makes a specific, measurable, or absolute claim about a product's ability to treat, cure, prevent, or alter a physical condition or appearance (such as reducing wrinkles, whitening teeth, or preventing acne) without providing the matching factual evidence and compliance sign-off. Unless the phrase is interpreted as a general description of difference or novelty rather than a superior or specific therapeutic outcome, and adequate evidence for that interpretation exists.
examples_good: Features a unique texture unlike any other on the market.
Contains a new ingredient blend for a fresh feel.
Designed to offer a different approach to daily care.
examples_bad: Clinically proven to eliminate dark spots in one week.
Prevents hair loss and restores full density.
Instantly whitens teeth by two shades.

wording.title: Regulated Efficacy Claims Require Evidence
wording.instruction: A sentence breaks this rule when it makes a specific claim about a product's ability to treat, prevent, or alter a physical condition or appearance (such as curing acne, lightening skin, or growing hair) without providing the specific factual evidence or compliance sign-off that validates that claim. Unless the claim is supported by robust, verifiable data (such as a cited survey or clinical study) that is explicitly referenced or attached to the copy, the sentence is non-compliant.
examples_good: According to a 2023 clinical trial, 90% of users saw reduced redness in 4 weeks.
Rated #1 by 500+ dermatologists in the UK, based on 2024 survey data.
Contains 2% salicylic acid, a clinically proven ingredient for exfoliation.
examples_bad: Clears up acne and reduces oiliness in just one week.
Instantly lightens dark spots and evens out skin tone.
Stops hair loss and promotes new growth naturally.

wording.title: Regulated Efficacy Claims Require Evidence and Sign-off
wording.instruction: Identify any claim that asserts a specific, measurable, or comparative health, cosmetic, or therapeutic outcome (e.g., reducing wrinkles, curing marks, softening skin, preventing pimples). Such claims must be supported by a matching factual basis and explicit compliance sign-off. Do not flag general descriptors of novelty, mechanism, or difference (e.g., 'new mode of action') unless they imply a superior or specific regulated result.
examples_good: A novel formulation designed to support skin hydration.
This product features a unique texture that feels smooth on the skin.
Contains ingredients known for their antioxidant properties.
examples_bad: Clinically proven to eliminate acne in 7 days.
Reduces the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles instantly.
Guaranteed to whiten teeth without sensitivity.

wording.title: Regulated Efficacy Claims Require Evidence and Sign-off
wording.instruction: Identify any claim that promises a specific physical change, medical benefit, or comparative superiority (e.g., removing blemishes, lightening skin, growing hair, or being 'more effective' than competitors). Such claims must be supported by a matching factual basis and explicit compliance sign-off. Do not flag claims based on third-party endorsements or survey data, provided they are backed by robust, consistent evidence.
examples_good: Rated #1 by 90% of users in a 2023 independent survey.
Contains 2% salicylic acid to help exfoliate skin.
Recommended by dermatologists for daily use.
examples_bad: Removes all blackheads in just one week.
Lightens dark spots and evens skin tone instantly.
More effective than leading brand X for hair growth.

wording.title: Regulated efficacy phrases need a matching fact and compliance sign-off
wording.instruction: Regulated efficacy phrases need a matching fact and compliance sign-off. This includes claims stating a specific result, a numerical value, a comparison, or a medical effect.
examples_good: Contains 2% salicylic acid.
New formula with added vitamin E.
Available in three shades.
examples_bad: Reduces fine lines in 7 days.
Twice as effective as leading brands.
Cures acne and prevents breakouts.

wording.title: Regulated efficacy phrases need a matching fact and compliance sign-off
wording.instruction: Regulated efficacy phrases need a matching fact and compliance sign-off. This includes claims of specific results (e.g., reduction, removal, growth), numerical outcomes (e.g., days, years), comparative superiority (e.g., more effective than), or medical/physiological effects (e.g., penetrates, regulates, lightens).
examples_good: Rated #1 by 90% of users in a 2023 independent survey.
Contains 2% salicylic acid to help exfoliate skin.
Formulated with hyaluronic acid for hydration.
examples_bad: Reduces wrinkles in just 7 days.
More effective than leading competitors.
Instantly plumps and firms the skin.
